skills.title: Create structured proposal document with comprehensive sections
steps: Organize the proposal into clearly labeled sections with hierarchical headings
Include all essential components: title, abstract, key topics, target audience, format/structure, speaker bio, and additional information
Provide formatting examples and alternative options for key sections (e.g., multiple title format examples)
Use bracketed placeholders for customizable content while maintaining professional structure
Specify word counts or length guidelines for sections like abstracts (150-250 words)
Include metadata sections like learning outcomes, prerequisites, and timing details
skills.evidence: The agent created a comprehensive talk proposal file with multiple well-organized sections including Talk Title (with examples), Abstract (with word count guidance), Key Topics & Learning Outcomes, Target Audience, Talk Format & Structure, Speaker Bio & Credentials, and Additional Information. The document used bracketed placeholders for customization while maintaining professional structure.
skills.description: Organize the proposal into clearly labeled sections with hierarchical headings

skills.title: Design proposal templates with actionable guidance
steps: Provide concrete examples for each major section to guide content creation
Include alternative formatting options to give flexibility in presentation style
Add instructional notes within brackets explaining what content should go in each section
Break down complex sections into subsections with specific prompts (e.g., primary/secondary audiences, prerequisites)
Specify practical details like timing, delivery style, and presentation flow
skills.evidence: The agent included "Alternative title format examples" with specific patterns, used bracketed instructions like "[Write a 150-250 word abstract that captures:]", and broke down sections into detailed subsections such as Target Audience with primary/secondary categories and prerequisites.
skills.description: Provide concrete examples for each major section to guide content creation

intent: Research and outline adaptation methods structure

memories.content: Research paper section openings should be concise, typically 2-3 sentences that establish need, introduce approaches, and motivate the structure.
memories.evidence: Human explicitly requested "write a short 2-3 sentence opening paragraph for this entire section. this is a research paper."

memories.content: When writing is already concise, further condensation should focus on removing redundant phrases and shortening constructions while preserving all essential information.
memories.evidence: Human requested to "make the opening paragraph slightly more concise" after the initial draft, leading to removal of redundant phrases like "enabling immediate responsiveness to shifting expertise" and condensing "in settings where" to "when."

skills.title: Iterative text refinement through targeted edits
steps: Identify the specific text segment that needs improvement based on feedback
Use Edit tool with replace_all=false to modify only the targeted portion
Focus on removing redundancy and condensing phrases while preserving core meaning
Verify that essential information remains intact after compression
skills.evidence: In Round 3, when asked to make the opening "slightly more concise," the agent used Edit with replace_all=false to target only the opening paragraph, removed redundant phrases like "enabling immediate responsiveness to shifting expertise," shortened constructions like "adaptation—short-term" to "—short-term," and condensed "in settings where" to "when" while maintaining all essential information.
skills.description: Identify the specific text segment that needs improvement based on feedback

skills.title: Research paper section opening structure
steps: Establish the need or problem that motivates the section
Introduce the main approaches or methods being presented
Motivate why these approaches are combined or how they complement each other
Keep the opening to 2-3 sentences with academic tone
skills.evidence: In Round 2, when asked to write an opening paragraph for a research paper section, the agent created a 3-sentence structure that: (1) established the need for agents to respond rapidly and consolidate knowledge, (2) introduced parameter-free vs parameter-based approaches, and (3) motivated their combination for evolving expertise.
skills.description: Establish the need or problem that motivates the section

skills.title: Locate existing project materials before creating new content
steps: Use Glob with multiple patterns to search for relevant existing files (*.md, *.tex, *.txt)
Use pattern matching with keywords related to the task (e.g., *parameter*, *adaptation*)
Read discovered files to understand existing content and structure
Incorporate or build upon existing materials rather than starting from scratch
skills.evidence: In Round 1, the agent systematically used Glob with patterns like "**/*.md", "**/*parameter*", "**/*adaptation*" to discover existing files, found subsection_parameter_free.md, read its content, and then built the outline incorporating this existing material rather than creating everything anew.
skills.description: Use Glob with multiple patterns to search for relevant existing files (*.md, *.tex, *.txt)

intent: Gather context about the paper topic and scope
